steps.title: Cabernet Sauvignon
steps.body: Stellenbosch Cabernet, especially from the slopes of the Simonsberg and Helderberg, combines ripe dark fruit with herbal, savoury notes and firm structure. Wards like Simonsberg-Stellenbosch and Jonkershoek Valley are known for it. Good examples age 15 to 20 years. Many call Stellenbosch South Africa's Cabernet capital.

steps.title: Pinotage
steps.body: Pinotage, a 1925 cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault, then called Hermitage, gives dark fruit, plum, mulberry and smoky notes. Kanonkop, in Simonsberg-Stellenbosch, is famous for it. A Cape blend is a red blend with a significant share of Pinotage, usually 30 to 70%, with Bordeaux grapes or Shiraz, giving South Africa its own blend style.

options: A red blend with a significant share of Pinotage
A white blend of Chenin and Sauvignon

steps.title: Old vines
steps.body: South Africa's Old Vine Project, started in 2016, certifies vineyards over 35 years old with a Certified Heritage Vineyards seal. Stellenbosch has old Chenin, Cinsault and Pinotage vines whose low yields give concentrated wines. The project has helped save many old vineyards from being replanted.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Stellenbosch is South Africa's Cabernet capital
Pinotage and Cape blends are its own styles
The Old Vine Project protects old vineyards
